description: Word goes down Sprocket Row faster than the Post: No. 9 is let again. By noon the pie-shop twins have passed your window twice. The woman from No. 7 comes in to return a chisel she borrowed from Hester Vane, and hangs it on its own hook above the bench as if she had done it many times. Behind the hook is a notebook's binding: marbled boards, a cloth spine, H. Vane inked inside the front board in a small upright hand. You take it down. Every page has been torn out at the stitching. "She was never without that," says the woman from No. 7, and stays to see whether you know which end of a chisel is which.

options.label: Prop the door open and let the Row look its fill.

success.text: By teatime the Row has decided you are thin, clever and probably not stopping, and the pie shop sends round a pie to test at least the first. The woman from No. 7 gives you her opinion of your Boiler. It is not high, but it is free, and she is right about the feed pump.

options.label: See No. 7 out, shut the door and chalk a sign on it: CLOSED FOR REPAIRS. OPINIONS BY APPOINTMENT.

success.text: The sign is read aloud the length of the Row before the chalk is dry, and improved twice by morning. Nobody calls. But the next day there is a tin of good oil on your step, with no note, and you understand that the Row has decided to wait and see. That is as close to a welcome as Sprocket Row gives anyone.
